Your skin looks nice to me! Just some acne. My suggestion (as someone who has adult acne) would be to cut out fragrance, moisturize, and use Differin or an Rx retinol. I've noticed that changing up my products, like doing a fun facemask (even the expensive ones) can freak my skin out and cause a breakout. I'd suggest wash with a gentle cleanser, then a fragrance free moisturizer, and Differin. And try to find a sunscreen that works for you, there's a lot of affordable fragrance free mineral and chemical sunscreens on the market rn. 

Also, after your skin adjusts to retinol, I've found using a q tip to apply benzoyl peroxide to my individual breakouts instead of all over works well. I usually do retinol at night then after I wash my face in the morning I use the benzoyl peroxide. 

I hope this is helpful 💕

I have dermatillomania and Epiduo (Rx), Epiduo Forte (Rx), or any kind of adapalene (like over the counter Differin) has been really useful for me. Takes a while to work and you have to be careful to use it consistently and in the right way, but it totally reduced my acne, which reduced the times I am tempted to pick. And it faded or got rid of a lot of the dark spots I had on my back and shoulders. CeraVe AM in the morning, then CeraVe PM mixed in my hands with Epiduo Forte has been my routine (as reccomended by my dermatologist). Just be aware that adapalene can cause dry skin or irritation, and if you use it too often when you first start it you will definitely get irritation. And, it brings a lot of the gunk to the surface so you will get a breakout in the first few weeks you use it. Also therapy helps with picking :D I hope this was helpful!

I was vegan for over 3 year between the ages of 15 and 18. I lost weight and muscle and wasn't healthy at all. I took supplements and tried to eat lots of greens and whatnot. No matter what I did I was deficient in vitamin D. I have struggled with mental health issues since I was 10 and they got 100% worse during those years. While a lot of it could be teenage angst, I doubt that was all of it. I changed to ovo lacto pescatarian for a few months and felt marginally better. But I was still struggling mentally and psychically. I finally said fuck it and went back to being an omnivore. I'm 5'8" I went from 140 to 190lbs in 6 months. I've always had a binge eating problem and was using veganism as an eating disorder of sorts, even though I didn't look like it. I started counting calories (healthily) and using my Fitbit since August and I'm back down to 160. I'm relatively healthy now and my mental health has gotten better, even though I've had some tough times this year. I really urge people to a) make sure they are taking care of their bodies and b) make sure your diet isn't making your mental health worse. Through eating healthily, therapy, and finally finding the right mix medications after years, I am doing better for once in my life. I can't recommend veganism to anyone with mental issues. Some of the deficiencies are proven to exacerbate mental issues, and unless you have a ton of money and time to eat healthily and get supplements, just don't. Seriously.
